component.name: Katakomba
component.summary: Route all traffic through a VPN over Tor

description.p: Katakomba routes all of your computer's traffic through WireGuard or OpenVPN, whose connection itself travels through the Tor network. Your VPN provider sees a Tor exit node, never your real address; your Internet provider sees Tor, never your VPN or where you go.

A background service manages Tor, WireGuard or OpenVPN, DNS and reconnections, and a setup wizard only needs the configuration files downloaded from your VPN provider: they are adapted for Tor automatically.

ul.li: Kill switch: nothing leaves outside the tunnel, even during reconnections
WireGuard through Tor for Proton VPN, Mullvad and IVPN, with OpenVPN as fallback
Automatic failover between accounts, transports and providers, and recovery after sleep
IPv6 blocking, the VPN's DNS applied on the tunnel, and split DNS for local domains
Built-in diagnostics that check routing, DNS and the real exit address
Desktop notifications when the connection drops and when it comes back
Advanced settings: network exclusions, LAN sharing, Tor circuit options

description.p: Requires a VPN provider offering OpenVPN over TCP, or WireGuard wrapped in TCP (Proton VPN, Mullvad, IVPN). Expect a few megabits per second: fine for browsing, less so for HD video.

screenshot.caption: Connection status and the path your traffic takes
VPN providers and accounts, in failover order

description.p: Managed WireGuard for IVPN: Katakomba registers its own WireGuard key on your IVPN account, through Tor, with no file to create.

ul.li: Built for fleets sharing accounts: one device slot per PC, kept across reboots, accounts drawn at random
Weekly key renewal on the same session, without taking another slot
A session closed at IVPN is noticed and replaced automatically; the slot is given back on uninstall
Optional reset of a full account, for accounts reserved for Katakomba
API exchanges run without any privilege; the account number is never stored in clear

description.p: Transport order per provider.

ul.li: Each provider can have its own order (for example WireGuard for one provider, OpenVPN for another), or follow the general setting
Set it on the Providers page, or with katakomba provider transports

description.p: WireGuard through Tor, alongside OpenVPN. Providers are dropping OpenVPN: Katakomba now carries WireGuard inside Tor too, wrapped in TCP the way each provider expects.

ul.li: Proton VPN (Stealth, TLS), Mullvad (udp-over-tcp) and IVPN (V2Ray, VMess) WireGuard files, recognised automatically
A provider can offer both: WireGuard first and OpenVPN as fallback by default, or the order of your choice in the settings
The bridge between WireGuard and Tor runs without any privilege; the private key only passes through a 0600 file deleted at once
Kill switch, DNS, exclusions, LAN sharing, watchdog and diagnostics work the same with both transports
Existing configurations keep working unchanged

description.p: Maintenance release with no change in behaviour: the packages now name their maintainer by a fixed pseudonym and an anonymous address.
Security fix: a crafted OpenVPN configuration file could hide a directive from Katakomba's checks, so that OpenVPN would load an external library. Such files are now rejected.

ul.li: Configuration files are now read exactly the way OpenVPN reads them
A malformed setting pushed by the VPN server no longer stops the tunnel from coming up
The diagnostics warn when the system network service would cut the tunnel each time it restarts
Every change is now checked against a real kernel and the real OpenVPN program

description.p: Maintenance release with no change in behaviour: every change to the code is now checked by static analysis tools, and a few dead imports and fragile shell constructs were cleaned up.
Fixes an endless reconnection loop reported by an administrator, after an automatic update restarted the system's network service.

ul.li: Routes and rules removed by systemd-networkd are put back within 30 seconds, without reconnecting
The address of the network card shared with the local network is put back too
After a failed restart of OpenVPN alone, the next step is always a full restart, with a growing delay between attempts so as not to exhaust the provider's simultaneous connections
A tunnel that sends without receiving anything is detected without waiting 30 seconds

description.p: Improvements reported by an administrator running Katakomba on about twenty machines.

ul.li: A monitoring tool can read the tunnel's status without being able to change the configuration
OpenVPN no longer warns at every connection that its credentials file is readable by a group
The diagnostics no longer report a failure when the account running them is not allowed to read the status

description.p: Fixes version 3.11.0, in which Tor could not start: the hardened service did not leave it the right to switch to its own unprivileged user. The hardening is otherwise unchanged.
The background service now runs with only the rights it needs, and every published package can be verified.

ul.li: The service can no longer load kernel modules, inspect other programs or write outside its own folders
Packages are built by GitHub from the published source, with checksums and a signed record of where they come from
Anyone can rebuild a package and get the very same file

description.p: Katakomba now runs on servers and machines without a screen. A separate package leaves out the graphical interface, and every setting can be changed from the command line.

ul.li: Incoming connections (SSH, web server) stay reachable once the tunnel is up; everything the machine sends itself still goes through the tunnel
Trial start for remote administration: the service stops by itself unless confirmed
The diagnostics check that replies to incoming connections leave outside the tunnel

description.p: OpenVPN no longer runs as root. It parses data received from the network; a flaw in it, or a malicious VPN server, could take over the machine. It now runs as a dedicated user with no privileges at all, and Katakomba sets up the tunnel itself.

ul.li: Routes pushed by the VPN server that would leave the tunnel are refused
Tor relay routes are always set before the tunnel routes
Only OpenVPN's own messages are recognised, never text sent by the server

description.p: Security fixes from an audit. The service no longer trusts its configuration file, which programs running in your session can edit.

ul.li: Exclusions towards the Internet are limited to /16: broader ones could take all traffic out of the tunnel
Local DNS settings are validated before being written into the system DNS configuration
DNS servers pushed by the VPN that would bypass the tunnel are ignored
The status socket is readable by Katakomba users only
Backups are size-checked and validated on import

description.p: Kill switch, on by default: while the service runs, nothing leaves outside the tunnel, even during reconnections. Only Tor itself, the local network, the local DNS server and the excluded networks bypass it. It is lifted when you disconnect.
Software centre metadata: Katakomba now shows its description, screenshots and release notes in GNOME Software and the Ubuntu App Center.
The package now depends on python3-gi-cairo: without it, the window crashed when opening on a minimal installation. The license is stated consistently as GPL-3.0.
New name: Katakomba. An installation made under the previous name is migrated automatically.

ul.li: Provider files are adapted for Tor automatically, as downloaded
Allowlists for OpenVPN and Tor configuration, Tor runs unprivileged
Faster recovery: OpenVPN alone is restarted when Tor is healthy
